**Canyon Strike** is implemented and `npm run build` succeeds (`tsc --noEmit` clean, Vite bundle emitted to `dist/`). The only build output note is Vite's standard >500 kB chunk advisory, which comes from bundling Three.js itself.

## What was built

**World** (`src/world/`) — an analytic, procedurally generated meandering canyon: the same height field drives both the chunked terrain mesh (sampled once into a shared grid, frustum/fog culled per chunk) and all collision queries, so what you see is what you hit. Layered strata vertex colouring, a river along the floor, rock spires, boulders, pines, five flyable rock arches, a shader sky dome with sun glow, drifting clouds and exponential fog.

**Flight** (`src/game/player.ts`) — arcade jet handling with throttle/afterburner, speed-dependent control authority, gravity-induced nose sag, energy bleed on climb, auto-coordinated rudder, gentle levelling assist, wingtip vapour under G, and afterburner cones that swell with throttle. Terrain impact and a soft mission-area boundary with a countdown are both loss conditions.

**Combat** (`weapons.ts`, `enemies.ts`) — instanced tracer cannon with convergence assist and heat management, lock-on missiles with proportional guidance, flare decoys, six primary strike targets (radar, depot, SAM battery, bunker, hangar, second radar), a defence net of SAM batteries and AAA emplacements with line-of-sight checks, and six interceptors spawning in waves with pursue/extend/evade AI and terrain avoidance.

**Feedback** — pooled GPU particle systems for fire, smoke, sparks, debris, shockwave rings…
